dedupe_keys.name: zero emission services zes battery container exchange and charging network for inland shipping netherlands

description: Zero Emission Services (ZES), a company founded by ING, ENGIE, Wärtsilä and the Port of Rotterdam Authority with support from the Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, runs a network of exchangeable battery containers (ZESpacks) and open access charging stations for electric inland vessels. Contents: the company pages give the station network and its figures (5 charging stations open and 3 upcoming in 2026, 2 ships sailing and 2 upcoming, conversion subsidy granted for 12 ships), the station sites (Alphen aan den Rijn, Alblasserdam, Den Bosch, Moerdijk, Rotterdam), and ZESpack specifications: a 20 ft container of 2,600 kWh, giving a barge 2 to 6 hours of sailing, exchanged in about 15 minutes, with two packs charged in parallel in 2.5 hours. Packs off board can stabilise the grid, store local solar or wind power or supply mobile shore power. Coverage: Dutch inland waterways and the Moerdijk seaport. Format and access: web pages only, no downloadable table. Licence and cost: pages free to read; no licence is stated. Caveats: figures are company statements and change as stations open. Useful for capacity planning and network flow models of electric inland shipping, battery logistics and port grid flexibility. It relates to the CBS inland shipping freight statistics and the Rhine 2018 low water case study in the catalogue.
